resale_co.name: Residential Sale / Re-Rent Certificate (Residential Resale Certificate)
resale_co.issued_by: Department of Code Enforcement, Zoning and Construction
requirements: Smoke alarm on each floor, including the basement, within 10 feet of all sleeping areas (the Borough sheet says alarms must be within 7 years of the manufacture date)
CO alarm within 10 feet of all sleeping areas, outside the rooms
Fire extinguisher mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen, ABC type, 2.5 to 10 pounds
Running water, working electric service and at least one flushable toilet
Handrails and guards on steps of 3 or more risers or 30 inches
Well water and/or septic report from the Board of Health, if applicable
Water heater grounded (jump bonded); relief discharge tube not reduced and ending within 6 inches of the floor
Solid aluminum dryer vent pipe, not flex pipe
Anti-tilt device on the stove
House numbers visible from the street
Exit doors open from inside without a key or special knowledge
No mold or water damage
Any outstanding Borough fines or liens paid in full
New owner's Resident Info (Police Department emergency file) form must be turned in before inspections are scheduled; the property will be photographed
Change of title only (vacant, not yet habitable home): floor plan layout of all floors

fees.label: Residential Sale / Re-Rent inspection, per unit

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in Sections 1 and 2 of the Borough's Residential Sale / Re-Rent Application (fillable PDF) and return them with the Middlesex Borough Police Department resident form (new buyer's information) and a check payable to Middlesex Borough for $125 to the Construction/Code Enforcement office, 1200 Mountain Avenue, Middlesex, NJ 08846. The smoke/CO part (Section 3) goes separately to the Middlesex County Fire Marshal; the Borough does not accept that form or its payment.
resale_co.contact_title: Director of Code Enforcement and Zoning

resale_co.notes: Required under Chapter 158, Article II of the Borough Code (per the application). The Construction page explains the Borough's certificate names: 'Residential Resale Certificate' for selling a home, 'Change of Title' for a vacant home that is not yet habitable. The application (fillable PDF on the Forms page under Zoning Board of Adjustment / Code Enforcement, file uploaded 2026-05-19) covers both sales and rental changes of occupancy; the application header gives the office line as 732-356-7400 ext. 247 (the Construction office line, Technical Assistant Karen Wick, construction@middlesexboro-nj.gov). The inspection checklist and fee pages of the packet are scanned images and were read visually; the $125 fee and the $50 Fire Marshal note are in the text layer. The checklist sheet says smoke alarms must be within 7 years of the manufacture date, while the County Fire Marshal guideline page in the same packet says 10 years (7 for stand-alone CO alarms). The checklist also says the property is subject to Ordinance 317-11 (property maintenance). No lead time, validity period or reinspection fee is printed. A search result still points to an older 2020 Borough resale form (FORM-CONSTRUCTION-Resale-Residential-Certificate-20200716.pdf); that file now returns 'not found' on the Borough site, so its fees were not used. The Director's cell number is on the page but is not recorded.

requirements: County letter: smoke alarms on every level (basement, first and second floors, not crawl spaces or unfinished attics) and within 10 feet of sleeping rooms; no older than 10 years or the maker's expiration date
County letter: CO alarm outside each separate sleeping area; no older than 5 years or the maker's expiration date (other County pages say 7 years for stand-alone CO alarms)
County letter: house numbers at least 4 inches high, visible from the street and in a contrasting color (2 inches if on both sides of a curbside mailbox)
County letter: smoke/CO alarms, house numbers and fire extinguisher must all comply; certificate is issued at the inspection and valid for 6 months
Smoke alarms within 10 feet of every bedroom and at least one on every floor, including finished and unfinished basements (not needed in an unfinished attic)
Smoke alarms may not be more than 10 years old; stand-alone CO alarms not more than 7 years old; combination alarms not more than 10 years old
A hard-wired smoke alarm must be replaced with a hard-wired alarm
A replacement battery smoke alarm must have a sealed 10-year lithium battery

Fire extinguisher (listed on the County form in the Borough's 2026 packet): 2-A:10-B:C, about 5 pounds, wall-mounted on the way out of the kitchen, no higher than 5 feet, with a receipt or NJ licensed contractor tag from the past 12 months
Homes built 1984 or later need interconnected electric alarms; homes built 1990 or later also need battery backup and an alarm in each bedroom

fire_cert.notes: The DCA July 2026 registry lists the County (code C) as the fire enforcing agency for Middlesex Borough ('Middlesex County is the LEA for Middlesex Boro'). The County Fire Marshal's own web pages could not be opened (the County site returned 403 Forbidden to plain requests), so the fee comes from the Borough's May 2026 resale packet ('$50 Fee will be payable to the Middlesex Fire Marshal') and the County's own 2020 application form (archived copy, linked from the Milltown Fire Department site; original URL http://www.middlesexcountynj.gov/Government/Departments/PSH/Documents/Fire-Marshal/Residential Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Inspection Info and Application.pdf). The 2020 County form was a temporary notarized self-inspection affidavit; the 2026 packet's County form is an inspector's application (Inspector/Date/Time fields), so a site inspection is now expected. The County form in the 2026 packet still has a Fire Extinguisher line and the guideline page still requires one, even though P.L.2025, c.19 removed the state extinguisher requirement; confirm with the Fire Marshal. The packet's County form gives the address as Sayreville, NJ 08879 (the 2020 form says 08872). The state directory lists (732) 316-7174 on this town's page and (732) 316-7171 on the County page; the County form uses 732-316-7171. Type is 'unknown' because the schema has no county option: the enforcing agency is the County Fire Marshal. Note: the state fire directory uses code 1211 for Middlesex Borough, which differs from the Watchdog code 1210. The County Fire Marshal's own fee letter ('To: All Real Estate Agencies/Home Owners', undated, citing Middlesex County Fire Marshal Ordinance 10-1811) is posted on the South River Borough website (https://www.southrivernj.org/DocumentCenter/View/856/Smoke-Detector--Carbon-Monoxide-Detector-Inspection-PDF); it is the enforcing agency's county-wide schedule, not a South River fee, and is cited here for that reason: $50.00 (10+ business days), $75.00 (under 10), $125.00 (under 4), $20.00 reinspection, $75.00 no-show, checks payable to the Office of the Fire Marshal, certificate valid 6 months. It still lists a fire extinguisher.
